conventions.convention: Full-space TV₂ is the smooth compactly supported test-field supremum on real L²; finite TV₂ does not require global L¹ integrability.

Positive levels use {u>t}; negative levels use {u<t}. Canonical sets are density-one representatives and boundaries are ambient topological boundaries. Hausdorff distance is zero for two empty sets and infinite when exactly one is empty.
Neumann TV counts interior variation; Dirichlet TV counts full-space variation of the zero extension. Zero extension for geometric level sets does not change the selected regularizer.
A source certificate satisfies A*p† ∈ ∂R(u†) in real Hilbert spaces. The first Bregman argument is the comparison point; the second carries the chosen subgradient.
Variational curvature compares compactly supported symmetric-difference perturbations for the selected perimeter. The obstacle curvature condition compares Ω with full-space competitors.

The geometric theorem assumes supplied global minimizers, Countable Choice, η<2√π for full-space/Dirichlet TV, and η<1/CΩ for Neumann TV. Dirichlet geometry additionally requires the stated obstacle curvature and exterior L² lower bound. Invisible Neumann means are subtracted.
The Bessel multiplier uses the unitary Fourier transform with phase exp(−2πix·ξ), giving the factor 1+4π²|ξ|².

load_bearing.statement: For every sequence αₙ>0 with αₙ→0, p_{αₙ,0}→p₀ strongly in Y and A*p_{αₙ,0}→A*p₀ strongly in X. The noisy certificates satisfy ‖p_{α,w}−p_{α,0}‖≤‖w‖/α and the corresponding adjoint bound.

Under its source, supplied-minimizer, noise-threshold and branch-specific obstacle hypotheses, almost every nonzero canonical level has uniform ambient two-sided density and common bounded support; whenever the corresponding level sets converge in measure, their canonical boundaries converge in Hausdorff distance.

Under the stated source condition, bounded noise-to-parameter ratio and supplied global minimizers, after the specified Neumann mean normalization a subsequence converges weakly in L² and strongly in L¹ on bounded domains or locally in L¹ in full space to a minimum-TV exact solution u₀, with A*p† ∈ ∂R(u₀).

Assume Countable Choice. Every finite-variation u ∈ L²(R²) admits controlled smooth compactly supported cutoffs vₖ=χₖu in BV∩L¹, converging in L², with limsup TV(vₖ)≤TV₂(u); the conclusion holds for every family satisfying the four stated cutoff conditions.

Assume Countable Choice. For finite-variation u ∈ L²(R²), every nonzero signed level has finite area, almost every applicable level has finite perimeter, and TV₂(u) is the sum of the positive-superlevel and negative-sublevel perimeter integrals.
Assume Countable Choice. For every nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz domain Ω ⊂ R², there is CΩ>0 such that ‖u−uΩ‖₂≤CΩ TV(u;Ω) for every u ∈ BV(Ω).

Assume Countable Choice. If Ω ⊂ R² is open, u ∈ L²(Ω;R), and TV₂(u;Ω)<∞, then each distributional derivative is a finite signed Radon measure, and the vector derivative has finite Radon variation with |Du|(Ω)=TV₂(u;Ω).
